node.text:
Sara Arjun, who became famous as the girl from the Clinic Plus ad, is now a leading actress in Bollywood, acting with Ranveer Singh and earning ₹1 crore per movie.

She is the daughter of actor Raj Arjun and started acting when she was very young. By age 5, she had done more than 100 ads, including Maggi and Clinic Plus, and became a popular child actor.

Her talent and screen presence impressed filmmakers early on. At age 6, she debuted in the Tamil film Deiva Thirumagal, earning praise for her acting.

Sara has acted in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, and Malayalam films. Her role as young Nandini in Ponniyin Selvan made her famous nationwide. With Dhurandhar, she became a mainstream Bollywood heroine and is seen as a future star.

node.text:
Sourav Joshi’s wedding has become a big hit on YouTube. His wedding videos are getting close to 1 crore views each within a short time.

Being India’s top vlogger, his audience follows every moment he shares. In India, YouTube pays creators around ₹2 to ₹10 lakh for 1 crore views, depending on ads and viewers.

This means Sourav Joshi is earning several lakhs from each wedding video through ads alone. What was a personal family event has now turned into viral content.

His wedding series proves how powerful a loyal audience can be. It also shows how creators today can earn more from digital platforms than many traditional media options.

node.text:
Jennifer Lopez never expected her green dress to make internet history. When she wore it at a big event, people everywhere started searching for her photos online.

Back then, Google mostly showed text results, not pictures. The searches became so huge that Google understood one thing clearly: people wanted images. This moment pushed Google to create a new tool to show photos easily.

That tool later became Google Images. A single fashion choice ended up changing how the internet works forever.

The dress was not just about style or glamour. It proved how pop culture can influence technology and create tools used by millions every day.

India’s aviation sector is moving into a new phase. As IndiGo deals with delays and pressure, the door is opening for big players like Ambani and Adani to step in.

node.text:
China has completed a huge underwater tunnel project beneath the Yellow River, showing its strong engineering power.

The 8 lane tunnel cost about $20 billion and cuts travel time from nearly 2 hours to just 20 to 30 minutes. To build it, engineers used the world’s biggest tunnel boring machine called Shanhe, which is 17.5 meters wide.

The underwater part of the tunnel is 3.29 km long, while the total length is 5.75 km, making it the widest underwater tunnel ever. The work was done in tough conditions with high water pressure and complex soil. Even then, the machine moved up to 18 meters each day.

The underwater section was finished in only 110 days. This tunnel will greatly improve traffic and city development.

node.text:
A Nigerian fraudster pulled off one of the boldest scams ever by tricking a Brazilian bank into paying $242 million for an airport that did not exist.

He pretended to be a powerful government official and convinced the bank that a new airport project in Nigeria would make them huge profits. The bank trusted him and kept sending money, believing the deal was real.

Years later, when another bank tried to buy them, they checked the records and found that the airport project was completely fake. The truth shocked everyone and the Brazilian bank collapsed because of the massive loss.

The scammer was arrested, jailed, and had most of his money taken away. This story shows how confidence and lies can create one of the world’s biggest scams.

A video from Iran is trending again because an engineer named Alaeddin Qassemi says he created a car that runs only on water.

He claims his modified Peugeot can go 900 km with 60 litres of water by turning water into hydrogen and using that gas as fuel. Many people online are shocked and excited, but scientists strongly disagree.

Experts say this idea breaks basic science rules. Splitting water into hydrogen needs a lot of energy, more than the car can produce on its own.

So a “water-only car” cannot work without another energy source. This same video has gone viral many times since 2016, but there is still no scientific report, patent, or official proof. Until proper tests confirm it, the car remains an unproven claim.
